btts_and_clean_sheet.rederivation_notes: My own chain, written from the four sampled rules texts (regulation 90+stoppage, ET/pens excluded, own goals to beneficiary) before opening the record: (1) each side's regulation goal intensity from opponent-adjusted chance volume/quality, lineup and keeper; (2) BTTS = P(H>=1)P(A>=1) corrected for dependence, so the binding quantity is the weaker side's lambda (concave 1-exp(-lambda)); (3) zero-inflation / failed-to-score clustering and score-state coupling after a first goal; (4) discrete shocks (penalty, red card, late keeper change); (5) incentive context for cup/two-leg ties and rotation in mismatches; (6) own-goal credit and the settlement window. Required inputs I expected: ratings, confirmed XI and keeper, set-piece route, penalty/referee propensity, rotation/stakes/aggregate state, cross-tier bridge for cup mismatches. The record matches stages 1-4 and 6 well (min-lambda framing, excess-FTS, trailing hazard are good). What differed: it never attaches soc.penalty_rate although stage s4 and the audit text depend on it; knockout/aggregate incentives are asserted in s5 but carried by no input; cup-mismatch inputs used in the handicap record are absent; some interactions restate single-input nonlinearities. Verified against rules text: window, ET exclusion, own-goal clause, and the honest admission that no postponement clause is visible in the BTTS texts.

findings.text: Officiating coverage is incoherent. category_coverage.officiating_rules cites ['soc.fouls_cards'], but input_audit marks soc.fouls_cards WEAK with the reason 'only referee penalty propensity matters and is covered under soc.penalty_rate, not here'. soc.penalty_rate exists in the catalog (it is in the first_to_score_event input list) but is not attached to any stage, interaction or category of this record. Stage s4 ('A penalty (about 75-80% conversion ...) is a near-guaranteed route for an otherwise blanked team') therefore has no usable input. Attach soc.penalty_rate (referee/VAR-shrunk) and drop the WEAK input as the sole officiating cover.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Stage s4 and officiating_rules coverage now cite soc.penalty_rate (referee/VAR-shrunk) instead of the WEAK soc.fouls_cards; added a referee/penalty required_data row feeding it. soc.fouls_cards stays audited WEAK.

findings.text: Stage s5 asserts 'Knockout ties with advancement incentives change the 90-minute goal process (cagey first legs)', and live series include KXCOPADELREYBTTS, KXISRSCUPBTTS, KXCOPADOBRASILBTTS, KXCONMEBOLSUDBTTS (the last sampled as a CONMEBOL knockout-type match). No input carries aggregate state, rotation, or stakes: soc.second_leg_aggregate_state, soc.rotation_index and soc.stakes_leverage exist in the catalog (used in match_result_3way) but are neither attached nor listed as a GAP. The one disclosed gap (situational_schedule_motivation) says rotation_index/stakes inputs are 'not attached here' without explaining why, then concludes no effect-size evidence exists; the cheaper fix is to attach them.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Attached soc.second_leg_aggregate_state, soc.rotation_index and soc.stakes_leverage to stage s4; situational_schedule_motivation changed from GAP to COVERED and the gap entry replaced by an effect-size uncertainty (rotation_stakes_effect_size); they are fed by the new referee/penalty and schedule data row.

findings.text: Cross-tier mismatch inputs are missing for cup BTTS series. In Copa del Rey / Israeli Cup / Copa do Brasil early rounds the weaker side's lambda can be tiny and poorly identified; the handicap record defines soc.cross_tier_strength_link and soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch for exactly this, but the BTTS record (where min(lambda) is the binding quantity) does not reference them.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:cross_tier_lambda_floor

findings.text: Interaction #1 (soc.xg_adjusted_ratings x soc.weaker_side_big_chance_creation, form 'concave') is the same statement as nonlinearity #1 (saturating 1-exp(-lambda) in ratings) and is not an interaction of two inputs. Interaction #5 asserts a set-piece threshold at which weaker-side P(score) 'stays near 0.55-0.6'; no source or derivation is given for these numbers and the text should be marked as hypothesis. Interaction #3 asserts the dependence 'flips by the 70th minute' without support.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Replaced interaction 1 (a restatement of nonlinearity 1) with weaker-side big-chance x opposing keeper multiplicative interaction; marked the 0.55-0.6 set-piece figure and the 70th-minute dependence flip as unsourced hypotheses in interactions 5 and 3.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: the event-stream data row lists fields red_card_flag and score_h/score_a with Understat as the free source. To my knowledge Understat shot/match pages expose shot minute, xG, situation and result (including own goal) but not red cards; score-before must be reconstructed by cumulating goals. Card/ejection timing needs another provider (API-Football/Opta). Also the 'Reg Time: Both Teams To Score' rules_evidence quote is a market title, not rules text, and cannot by itself establish the window (the other quote does).
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:event_source_red_cards

findings.text: Archetype name is 'btts_and_clean_sheet' but no live clean-sheet series exists in the ledger and the record never states this; KXSOCCERBTTS (filed under handicap_and_exact_score) and KXUCL1HBTTS (filed here but a half market) are mis-bucketed neighbours. Own-goal credit is argued to add ~3-5% of goals to P(team scores) in variants_and_edge_cases but no input measures own-goal propensity (defender error / high line / crossing volume).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Recorded series_mapping_issues for KXSOCCERBTTS, KXUCLBTTS (belong here) and KXUCL1HBTTS (half market); added explicit statement that no clean-sheet series is live and that claims are conditional; own-goal propensity gap logged as unresolved own_goal_propensity_input (not an input).

competition_head_to_head.rederivation_notes: My own chain, before reading the record: a head-to-head season-finish contract is P(points_A_final > points_B_final) (+ tiebreak branch), driven by (1) current table state and games in hand; (2) each side's remaining fixtures via a calibrated match model with rating uncertainty that persists over the horizon (so gap sd grows roughly linearly, not with sqrt n); (3) negative covariance through direct meetings and positive through common opponents/shocks; (4) squad/manager shocks, cup/Europe load; (5) tiebreak order and any deduction; (6) settlement metric ambiguity (final table vs on-pitch points vs cup progression vs match result). Before opening the record I searched the ledger for live series and found three head-to-head series filed under match_result_3way: KXEPLH2HFINISH 'EPL H2H Finishing Position', KXEPLH2H 'EPL H2H Results', KXWCTEAMH2H 'World Cup Team Head to Head' (all TITLE_ONLY). The record's mechanism for season finish is sound and well matched to my chain (state, schedule asymmetry, paired correlation, tie branch). What differed: its foundational premise 'No live Kalshi series maps to this archetype' / NO_LIVE_SERIES is false, so it never separates the three actual contract variants (finish position vs match/results head-to-head vs World Cup team progress) and proposes retiring the archetype; several numeric claims are unsupported and one nonlinearity contradicts an interaction.

findings.text: Contract premise is wrong. contract.rules_verification='NO_LIVE_SERIES' and unresolved no_live_series_h2h says 'No Kalshi series maps to head-to-head in the ledger ... confirm that none exist and retire the archetype'. The evidence ledger does contain three live head-to-head series, mis-bucketed under match_result_3way: KXEPLH2HFINISH ('EPL H2H Finishing Position'), KXEPLH2H ('EPL H2H Results') and KXWCTEAMH2H ('World Cup Team Head to Head'), all TITLE_ONLY. The record must be re-based on these (state that rules are unseen, that 'Results' may be a different metric from finishing position, and that the World Cup variant is a tournament-progress comparison, not a table race). The recommendation to retire the archetype should be reversed and the mis-bucketing logged.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct on the premise; settlement_definition rewritten around the three live H2H series (KXEPLH2HFINISH, KXEPLH2H, KXWCTEAMH2H), retire recommendation removed, mis-filing logged in contract.series_mapping_issues, rules-unseen gap recorded as h2h_series_rules_unseen. rules_verification stays NO_LIVE_SERIES because the ledger holds none under this key.

findings.text: Three distinct contracts are collapsed into one table-race mechanism. KXEPLH2H 'Results' may settle on the two clubs' direct match results or points in direct meetings (zero-sum, two fixtures), which needs a match-outcome model rather than a season Monte Carlo; KXWCTEAMH2H needs a bracket/group-path model (soc.bracket_path_difficulty exists in the competition_winner record). variants_and_edge_cases mentions 'cup head-to-head' only hypothetically; stages s1-s5 and all three new inputs assume a league table finish.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:h2h_three_mechanisms

findings.text: Unsupported numerics presented as fact: 'sd about 1.6 points per sqrt(match)' (a 3-way points lottery with typical probabilities has per-match sd nearer 1.2-1.4), 'P(equal points) about 6-12%', and 'up to roughly 0.1 goals per match in the congested window' (interaction 3). They should carry a basis or be marked hypothesis.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Stage s2 per-match points sd corrected to ~1.2-1.4 and marked to-be-estimated; stage s5 P(equal points) and interaction 3 congestion effect rewritten as unsourced hypotheses to be measured rather than facts.

findings.text: Internal inconsistency: nonlinearity #2 says rating uncertainty gives 'Linear growth of variance with horizon', while interaction #5 (same input pair) says 'the sd of the gap grows more like linear in games remaining rather than sqrt'. With a persistent latent strength the sd (not the variance) is linear in n and variance is quadratic; the two entries cannot both be right and the test (coverage of simulated gap intervals) should name which.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Nonlinearity 2 and interaction 5 made consistent: persistent latent strength gives sd linear (variance quadratic) in games remaining, match noise gives variance linear; test now separates the two terms.

findings.text: Settlement variants omit non-standard finish formats the ledger shows elsewhere: Ecuador LigaPro hexagonal with carried-over points, Peru/Uruguay/Venezuela playoffs, MLS conferences (KXMLSEAST/KXMLSWEST are also in the winner bucket). For 'finish ahead' markets in such leagues the compared metric (aggregate table, stage table, playoff result) must be recorded as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS. The record also claims 'La Liga head-to-head first, Premier League goal difference first' without a source.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:h2h_format_variants

findings.text: coaching_scheme is disclosed as GAP while no mid-season manager-change input is defined; acceptable disclosure, but the gap is twice duplicated (gap_coaching_scheme and mid_season_manager_effect) and neither is tied to an input that would be added. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: ClubElo is listed as a rating source for 'ratings and uncertainty' but publishes point ratings only; the uncertainty (sd) field in the data row would have to be self-derived.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Merged the duplicated manager-change entries into one gap_coaching_scheme unresolved item and corrected the ClubElo source note (point ratings only, sd self-derived); no manager-change input is defined, gap kept and disclosed.

competition_winner_and_top_n.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the sampled texts (league champion binaries; KXECULP/KXPERLIGA1/KXURYPD/KXVENFUTVE describe two-stage or playoff formats; PointMargin series settle on first-minus-second with 0 on a tie; KXSOCCERTROPHIES sums four named competitions; KXBRASILEIROTOPX is a rank threshold): (1) latent team strength with persistent uncertainty and drift; (2) remaining fixtures simulated into a joint table; (3) format conversion (playoffs, split seasons, Apertura/Clausura finals, knockout draws, two-leg ties, penalties); (4) squad/manager shocks and cross-competition priority; (5) order statistics for margin and cut-line density for top-N; (6) administrative events (deductions, stripped titles). For the UEFA/WC props that make up much of the 124-series bucket (KXUCL16, KXUCL8, KXUCLADVANCE, KXUCLTOP/BOTTOM, KXUCLQUAL, KXUCLFINALIST, KXWCGROUPORDER, KXWCWINGROUP) I additionally expect a league-phase/group table simulation with the competition's own tiebreakers feeding a seeded bracket. The record matches stages 1-6 for domestic leagues and cups and is honest that the bucket is mixed. What differed: no mechanism or input for the UEFA 36-team league phase / playoff round / seeded bracket, none for a cross-league strength link although the data row carries a league_strength field, and rating sources for the South American leagues sampled are unverified.

findings.text: Missing mechanism for UEFA competitions. A large share of this bucket is UCL/UEL stage markets (KXUCL16*, KXUEL16* x8, KXUCL8, KXUCLADVANCE, KXUCLFINALIST, KXUCLTOP, KXUCLBOTTOM, KXUCLQUAL, KXUCLLEAGUE, KXTEAMSINUCL). Stage s3 converts table position to a title only through 'bracket with seeding' and 'soc.playoff_format_conversion' estimated from 'P(champion | seed rank)' over 10 seasons; it does not model the league-phase table (8 league matches against unequal opponents, top-8 direct / 9-24 playoff / 25+ out, tiebreakers) that determines seeding and bracket side. Historical conversion tables cannot be used because this format is new. A league-phase simulation input and a seeded-bracket-path-given-finish input are required.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Added new inputs soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation and soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish (36-team league-phase table simulation and rank-conditional bracket path), attached to stage s3 with required_data feed and UEFA.com source; format-history shortage logged as uefa_format_history_short.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED / undisclosed data gap. The rules-sampled series are dominated by Paraguay, Uruguay, Peru, Venezuela, Ecuador, Chile, Argentina and Copa Libertadores/Sudamericana outrights. Ratings are said to come from 'ClubElo (free)' and 'Understat/FBref xG'; to my knowledge ClubElo is European-centred and Understat covers six European leagues, so neither verifiably covers these clubs, and football-data.co.uk does not carry most of them. The unresolved list has no entry for rating-source coverage of non-European leagues, although the title/top-N inputs (soc.ratings, soc.ratings_uncertainty, soc.preseason_prior) all hinge on it.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:rating_source_coverage_non_european

findings.text: Series mis-mapping is disclosed but its consequence for the input list is not. The record notes KXUCLBTTS and World Cup player props, but the bucket also holds match-level contracts under outright_futures: KXGERSCGAME, KXCANPLGAME, KXUCLGAME, KXUCLWGAME, KXUCL1H, KXUCLSPREAD, KXEFLCHAMPIONSHIPSPREAD/TOTAL, KXUCLTOTAL, KXWCTEAMTOTALGOALS, KXWCGSGOALS, KXWCKOPENALTIES, KXWCCONCEDE1ST. 'Re-map each of the 124 series' is left as a future action; the record should say which inputs are valid for which contract subset and which series have no applicable input in this key at all.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Added input-scope statement to variants (inputs valid only for outright/top-N/advance/stage and margin series; none applicable to match-level or event/player props) and logged 19 misfiled tickers with target archetypes in contract.series_mapping_issues.

findings.text: Rules-text claims. The Ecuador (KXECULP) rules describe a hexagonal that carries over regular-season points and decides the champion on total points, Peru describes playoff/Apertura-Clausura, Venezuela a final between half-season winners; variants_and_edge_cases names Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, Liga MX and MLS but not these three, so the 'champion' definition varies more than stated. The Spanish Supercopa (a multi-team tournament inside KXSOCCERTROPHIES) is also not noted. The 'Manchester City-type cases' retroactive-sanction example is a judgment, not from the text.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Added Ecuador hexagonal with carried points, Peru Apertura/Clausura plus playoff, Venezuela half-season final and the Spanish Supercopa multi-team tournament to variants; labelled the Manchester City retroactive-sanction case as a judgement not drawn from rules text.

findings.text: Role/label issues: soc.xg is audited WEAK ('used only through ratings') yet is the only input cited for efficiency_conversion; soc.motivation is audited as circular yet cited for situational_schedule_motivation; soc.ratings_uncertainty x soc.comp_sim (interaction #1) pairs an input with the engine that consumes it and duplicates nonlinearity #1 (convex title odds in posterior width).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Efficiency cover moved from WEAK soc.xg to soc.ratings, situational cover from circular soc.motivation to soc.cup_progression_load, and interaction 1 replaced by preseason_prior x ratings_uncertainty (the old pair duplicated nonlinearity 1).

findings.text: KXSOCCERTROPHIES requires the joint distribution of four title events for one club; the record mentions a 'shared squad-fatigue state' but defines no input for dependence between a club's league, cup and Champions League outcomes, and s3 'w_r = P(win 90)+P(draw)*0.5 ... tilted 0.52-0.55' is unsupported.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Added new input soc.club_multi_competition_dependence (joint league/cup/UCL title dependence for KXSOCCERTROPHIES) fed from squad data and attached to stage s4; the unsupported 0.52-0.55 tilt now flagged as unresolved extra_time_tilt_unestimated and s3 favourite win-probability range marked hypothesis.

first_half_and_period.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the 18 sampled rules: half markets count only that half's goals (1H winner/Tie/2H Tie state 'after 45 minutes plus stoppage time'; total/spread/BTTS texts say only 'Only goals scored during the 1st Half count'; 1H exact score is a custom 'X wins 3-2' rung; Tie includes 0-0). Chain: (1) full-match team intensities; (2) share of scoring in the half by team/opponent/competition (about 44-46% of goals in the 1H) and the half's exposure including added time; (3) low-count joint distribution with large P(0-0) and draw mass; (4) for 2H, conditioning on the half-time score and any 1H red card; (5) lineup/news timing; (6) settlement variants and postponement. Required inputs I expected: ratings, lineups, period split, half-level dependence, score-state multipliers, added time, penalty/red-card propensity. The record covers these well and the half-level rho and state-multiplier inputs are good additions. What differed: three inputs estimate the same 1H/2H time-profile quantity and are all primary; free-source coverage of goal minutes/xG-by-minute is far narrower than the ~60 competitions of the 268 series; the stoppage-time claim in the contract summary is stated as verified for markets whose text does not say it; no entry for extra-time behaviour in cup 2H markets.

findings.text: Triple-counted time-profile input with inflated roles. soc.period_split (audited KEEP_PRIMARY, 'share of goals in each half'), new soc.half_specific_xg_ratings (primary; 1H/2H xG multiplier shrunk to the league 1H/2H ratio) and soc.first_goal_hazard (KEEP_SECONDARY, 'exactly the first-half time profile') all measure how a team's scoring is distributed across the match. The record itself says 'overlaps partially' for pace_press but never flags this overlap, and gives team-level sd of only ~4 percentage points around the league share with k=20 shrinkage, i.e. a small, noisy signal that should be secondary or context, not two primaries. Merge or demote.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Demoted the triple-counted time-profile inputs: soc.half_specific_xg_ratings new_input role primary to secondary with an overlap note, soc.period_split audit KEEP_PRIMARY to KEEP_SECONDARY, soc.first_goal_hazard KEEP_SECONDARY to KEEP_CONTEXT; soc.xg_adjusted_ratings remains the only primary.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED and undisclosed coverage gap. soc.half_specific_xg_ratings (primary) and soc.second_half_state_multiplier rely on shot-level xG with minute (Understat, six European leagues) and goal minutes; the data row lists football-data.co.uk first for fields goal_minute/goal_side, but to my knowledge football-data.co.uk provides half-time and full-time scores, not goal minutes. The live series span Liga Portugal, Taca de Portugal, Liga MX, MLS, USL, Eredivisie, Brasileiro, CONMEBOL, Coupe de France etc. Nothing in unresolved says that, outside the top-6 leagues, only HT/FT scores are available and half_specific xG cannot be computed; the BTTS record disclosed the same problem, this one does not.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:half_xg_coverage_non_top6

findings.text: Settlement overstated. The contract text and rules_verification=VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT state that every half market is 'the half's regulation 45 minutes plus its own stoppage time'. Only the winner/Tie markets (KXEREDIVISIE1H, KXSERIEA2H, KXUECL1H) say 'after 45 minutes plus stoppage time'; the 1H/2H total, spread and BTTS texts say only 'Only goals scored during the 1st/2nd Half count', and the exact-score texts have no secondary text at all. Inclusion of stoppage-time goals for those variants is inferred. The record also never raises whether a '2nd Half' market in a knockout cup (KXTACAPORT, KXUSOPENCUP, KXFACUP series exist) excludes extra-time halves; this is undisclosed CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:cup_second_half_extra_time

findings.text: Unsupported factual numbers: 'added time 1-3 minutes first half, 4-8 second half' (recent top-league first-half added time is typically longer than 1-3 minutes), '+25% for the trailing side, -15% for a two-goal leader', 'positive dependence of halves in strong-favourite matches and negative in tight ones', and the +7% exposure claim in the added_time interaction. Treat as hypotheses; the stage text presents them as facts.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Removed or relabelled unsupported numbers: stoppage lengths in the KXSERIEA2H evidence and stage s5, the +25%/-15% multipliers and halves-dependence sign in stage s4 are now hypotheses; interaction 4 +7% claim removed.

findings.text: Interaction quality: #3 (half_level_dependence_rho x draw_propensity) is a parameter-confounding statement, not an interaction of two inputs; #4 (added_time x period_split, form 'threshold') is described as a linear exposure shift, and nonlinearity #3 calls added_time 'Linear' so no threshold exists. #2 (press x opponent line height) needs opponent line-height data that no data row provides (Understat gives PPDA, not line height).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Replaced interaction 3 (parameter confounding) with first_goal_hazard x second_half_state_multiplier conditional chain; interaction 4 relabelled multiplicative to match nonlinearity 3; interaction 2 now uses an opponent PPDA/deep-block proxy available from Understat instead of unavailable line height.

findings.text: Cross-reference noise: the referee added-time data row lists feeds_inputs m.ladder_structure and m.rules_text, which are not fed by referee data; soc.xg is audited DUPLICATE_OF soc.xg_adjusted_ratings but is still cited in stage s1 and talent_strength coverage. Penalty/red-card propensity (soc.penalty_rate, referee) is absent although a first-half red card is named as a 2H driver in stage s4.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Removed m.ladder_structure and m.rules_text from the referee added-time feeds, replaced the duplicate soc.xg by soc.xg_adjusted_ratings in stage s1/talent coverage, and added soc.penalty_rate (with a referee/penalty required_data row) to s4 and officiating coverage.

first_to_score_event.rederivation_notes: My own chain, formed from the ledger before opening the record: all 42 live series are Method of Victory (KX*MOV) or Method of Finish (KX*MOF) plus KXWCLONGESTPEN, all TITLE_ONLY, so no settlement is visible. Notably MOV exists for domestic league games (KXLALIGAMOV, KXSERIEAMOV, KXBUNDESLIGAMOV, KXLIGUE1MOV, KXBRASILEIROMOV, KXLIGAMXMOV) that cannot go to extra time, while MOF appears only for knockout competitions; that pattern suggests MOV and MOF are two different contracts (MOV plausibly a margin/type-of-win split, MOF plausibly regulation/ET/penalties) rather than one path tree. The real First Team to Score series (about 30, KXAFCCLFTTS sampled: 'the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)', own goal to the awarded team) are filed under player_season_leader_and_awards, and KXWCFTTS/KXWCTTSF under handicap_and_exact_score. Chain for FTTS: competing-risk race of two time-varying intensities over 90 plus ET, no-goal outcome, route mix, early-goal bias. Chain for path-type contracts: regulation result, draw gate, ET process, shootout. The record covers both chains competently and is candid that nothing is verified; what differed is that it treats MOV and MOF as the same ET/penalty tree, so its mechanism is not validated by the league series, and FTTS inputs are described for a bucket that has no FTTS series.

findings.text: Unverified mechanism assumption drives the whole stage chain. The record assumes 'the three outcomes are plausibly win in regulation, win in extra time and win on penalties' for both Method of Victory and Method of Finish, and builds s1-s4, soc.knockout_cagey_factor, soc.method_path_tree_calibration and the shootout inputs on that. Its own variants note that six MOV series are domestic league fixtures (KXLALIGAMOV, KXSERIEAMOV, KXBUNDESLIGAMOV, KXLIGUE1MOV, KXBRASILEIROMOV, KXLIGAMXMOV) where extra time cannot occur, and that MOF exists only for knockouts. The unresolved item mov_mof_semantics lists the ambiguity but nothing in the record separates the two contract families or provides the alternative input set (a goal-margin distribution, shared with handicap_and_exact_score). The input list for the MOV league series is therefore unsupported. Fetch rules before relying on any of s2-s4.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:mov_league_outcome_set

findings.text: Archetype/series mis-mapping leaves the key without its named contract. No First Team to Score series lives in this bucket (the roughly 30 KX*FTTS series are in player_season_leader_and_awards, KXWCFTTS/KXWCTTSF in handicap_and_exact_score), so the FTTS-specific inputs (soc.first_goal_hazard primary, soc.first_goal_route_mix, soc.set_pieces, soc.penalty_rate) are validated against no series here. The sampled sibling rule (KXAFCCLFTTS) counts the 'entire game ... any extra time', so the FTTS race window is up to 120 minutes in knockouts; stage s5 describes only a regulation race and P(no goal) 'higher in cup ties' without modelling ET. The record discloses the mismatch (archetype_mismatch) but leaves the key serving two incompatible contracts; it should be split or re-bucketed before the input list is used.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Logged 32 FTTS series (plus KXWCLONGESTPEN) in contract.series_mapping_issues as belonging here or to a new archetype, stated that FTTS-specific inputs have no live series under this key, and added the extra-time window (entire game, up to 120 minutes) from the KXAFCCLFTTS text to variants and stage s5; ftts_window_not_in_this_bucket recorded.

findings.text: soc.second_leg_aggregate_state, soc.extra_time_shootout_model and soc.penalty_shootout_skill are used as stage inputs (s2-s4) and in interactions but are neither in this archetype's existing inputs, nor audited, nor defined in new_inputs; their measurement and sources are therefore unreviewed. Stage s3 states ET figures (0.4-0.5 goals, ~50% goalless) and s4 first-kicker win rates (53-60%) without sources.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:inputs_unaudited_in_archetype

findings.text: KXWCLONGESTPEN (a tournament extreme-value event) is excluded in variants, yet shootout inputs and required_data (15 seasons of knockout records) are still sized for it. Required-data coverage is also unaddressed: RSSSF/Wikipedia scraping gives ET/penalty flags, but the ClubElo/Understat strength sources cover European clubs only while MOF/MOV series include AFC Champions League, Copa del Rey amateur rounds, US Open Cup, Club World Cup (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for non-European ratings).
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:rating_source_coverage_cups

findings.text: Interactions: #5 (method_path_tree_calibration x xi_strength_delta) asserts a depleted favourite 'has a smaller drop in ET win' because ET depends on bench depth; no evidence is given. #2 is a product of probabilities (P(draw at 90) x P(ET draw)), i.e. a structural identity rather than an interaction between inputs. #4 (home_advantage x ratings, 'multiplicative') assumes the first-scorer odds fall by 'several percentage points' on neutral grounds without support.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Interaction 2 relabelled multiplicative and flagged as a structural identity used as a gate; interaction 5 marked as an unsupported hypothesis and interaction 4 magnitude changed to a quantity to estimate from neutral-venue finals.

findings.text: audit: soc.pace_press and soc.shots are WEAK yet pace_volume is marked COVERED using exactly those two inputs; with both discounted the category is effectively uncovered and should be GAP or NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: pace_volume reclassified from COVERED (by the WEAK inputs soc.pace_press and soc.shots) to NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason that volume enters through soc.xg_adjusted_ratings and soc.first_goal_hazard; the WEAK inputs are no longer cited.

handicap_and_exact_score.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the 7 sampled texts: spreads are 'X wins by more than N.5 goals ... after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)' so P(margin >= ceil(N.5)) on regulation goal difference; exact-score rungs are 'X wins 5-2' on the 90-minute score. Chain: (1) strength gap with a cross-tier bridge for cup mismatches and women's leagues; (2) favourite's lineup/rotation and the starting XI; (3) goal-difference distribution with thick right tail from blowouts and garbage-time damping; (4) joint cell structure for exact scores (low cells via dependence, high cells via overdispersion); (5) red-card/early-goal regimes; (6) nested ladder consistency and regulation-only settlement. Required inputs: ratings with uncertainty, tier link, rotation/lineups, home advantage, goal-count distribution calibration, tail inflation. The record matches this chain closely and its cross-tier, rotation and tail inputs are good. What differed: it asserts every correct-score series settles at 90 minutes although the ledger holds KXWCSCOREET ('Correct Score after Extra Time'); some rules_evidence 'establishes' statements go beyond the text and contradict its own unresolved note about rung structure; the bucket contains first-team-to-score and BTTS series it does not mention; women's and amateur-tier rating data are unaddressed.

findings.text: Settlement claim contradicted by the ledger. The contract states correct-score series are 'settled on the 90-minute final score' and the key target says 'in regulation'. The bucket contains KXWCSCOREET titled 'Correct Score after Extra Time' (TITLE_ONLY) plus KXWCEVERYTEAMGOAL, KXWCFTTS and KXWCTTSF (first-team-to-score) and KXSOCCERBTTS, all typed correct_score here. An ET-inclusive score requires the extra-time goal process and shootout/ET path inputs that exist only in the first_to_score_event record; the record neither mentions KXWCSCOREET nor lists the window as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:exact_score_et_window

findings.text: rules_evidence 'establishes' text exceeds the quotes. For KXUEFANLSCORE the quote 'If Switzerland wins 5-2 in the Switzerland vs North Macedonia professional UEFA Nations League soccer game' is said to establish that 'the ladder sums to one over all scorelines' and that 'a 7-goal match is a single rung'; the unresolved item exact_score_rung_set correctly says draw/other rungs are not visible, contradicting that claim. For KXFRAPLWSPREAD the quote shows only the 5.5 strike, not 'a mismatch event, not Poisson noise'; KXCOPADELREYSCORE does not show 'amateur sides'. These are inferences presented as rule content.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Rewrote the establishes text for KXUEFANLSCORE, KXFRAPLWSPREAD and KXCOPADELREYSCORE so each states only what the quote shows and labels the rest as inference; the partition claim now points to exact_score_rung_set.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: soc.cross_tier_strength_link is primary and lists ClubElo plus football-data.co.uk cup results. Sampled spread/score series include Coupe de France tie between a semi-professional and a regional club (IS-Selongey), Copa del Rey first-round amateur side (UD Maracena) and French Women's Premiere Ligue (PSG vs Le Havre, 5.5 strike); to my knowledge neither source rates tier 6+ or women's clubs. The cup_bridge_identifiability item covers amateur sides but women's-league coverage is not mentioned, although KXFRAPLWSPREAD is one of the few sampled spread texts.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:cross_tier_source_coverage

findings.text: soc.fouls_cards is audited WEAK, then used as an input to stage s5 'Ladder consistency and settlement' (a deterministic mapping stage) and as sole cover for officiating_rules; the event-stream data row feeds soc.set_piece_matchup from a goal/red-card log. Red-card/early-goal regimes are named in the interaction on blowouts but no red-card propensity input (referee, team indiscipline) exists.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Removed WEAK soc.fouls_cards from stage s5 and officiating cover and from the event-stream feeds; attached soc.referee and soc.penalty_rate to stage s3 with a referee/penalty required_data row; event-stream fields now include situation (feeds set_piece_matchup) and red_card_minute.

findings.text: Interaction #5 (home_advantage x lineups_pit: 'a rotated home favourite loses much of its crowd-driven edge') and #4 (league_strength_dispersion x ratings_uncertainty 'convex') are asserted without evidence; the test for #4 compares calibration by league balance but the dispersion statistic is computed from the same ratings model it is meant to correct, so the contrast is partly circular. soc.league_strength_dispersion could equally be a context variable only.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Interactions 4 and 5 labelled as hypotheses, interaction 4 test now uses an external table-based balance statistic instead of the ratings model (removing circularity), and soc.league_strength_dispersion role demoted from secondary to context.

findings.text: Rotation predictor (soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch) is labelled primary with pregame_knowable 'partial' and its own unresolved item says no free point-in-time rotation signals exist (rotation_ground_truth). A primary input with no backtestable history should be flagged as such in its role or fed by the one verifiable proxy (previous-match XI changes, fixture density), which the measurement does not actually restrict itself to.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch role changed from primary to secondary and its measurement restricted to verifiable point-in-time proxies (previous XI changes, rest days, fixture density), with unverifiable press-conference signals excluded from backtests.

match_result_3way.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the 12 sampled texts: three binaries per match ('Tie is the result' / team wins) settled on '90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)', fair-price resolution if cancelled or rescheduled beyond 48 hours. Chain: (1) team strength differential and venue/home advantage; (2) who actually plays (confirmed XI, keeper, rotation); (3) fatigue/travel/altitude and stakes; (4) draw mass from goal environment and low-cell dependence; (5) discrete shocks (penalties, red cards); (6) competition-specific incentives (two-leg state, friendlies, dead rubbers). Required inputs: ratings, home advantage, XI/lineup vintage, rest/travel/altitude, stakes/rotation, referee, aggregate state, draw propensity. The record matches this and adds good items (lineup surprise, altitude gap, friendly intensity). What differed: the bucket is not a match-result bucket (I count about 40 league/cup/World Cup winner outrights, three head-to-head contracts, a cricket World Cup and an MLS skills challenge among 185 series) and the record only admits spread/total; soc.market_odds is smuggled into coverage; the altitude threshold is inconsistent across three places; weather is deferred to 'other archetypes'.

findings.text: Undisclosed mis-bucketing. The contract says only 'same-event Spread and Total series (KXARGPREMDIVSPREAD, KXARGPREMDIVTOTAL)' share the bucket. The ledger's live_series also place here: KXEPLH2H, KXEPLH2HFINISH, KXWCTEAMH2H (head-to-head contracts, which belong to competition_head_to_head), about 25 league/cup/World Cup winner outrights (KXEREDIVISIE, KXLIGAMX, KXCOPADELREY, KXMWORLDCUP, KXMENWORLDCUP, KXUECL, KXTACAPORT, KXKLEAGUE, KXEFLCUP, KXKNVBCUP, ...), group/World Cup props (KXWCGROUPWINNER, KXWCGAMEGOALS, KXWCLOCATION, KXWCPLAY, KXWCWINNERTRAIL), KXMLSSKILLS, KXT20WORLDCUP and KXWT20WORLDCUP (cricket), and match-day spread-named series (KXFACUPSPREAD, KXSAUDIPLSPREAD, KXBRASILEIROSPREAD, KXLIGAMXSPREAD, KXTACAPORTSPREAD) whose settlement is TITLE_ONLY. Roughly a fifth of the bucket is not a regulation 3-way result; the unresolved list should say so and the record's settlement/input claims should be scoped to the GAME series.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:bucket_mixed_contracts

findings.text: Market-derived value counted as coverage. soc.market_odds is correctly audited BENCHMARK_ONLY, but it is also the second input cited for settlement_contract coverage (['m.rules_text','soc.market_odds']), a stage-s6 input, and listed in feeds_inputs of the referee data row. A benchmark must not be an input to any stage or category; settlement_contract is covered by m.rules_text alone. Likewise the referee dataset (penalties/reds/yellows) is not a feed for soc.market_odds or m.rules_text.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Removed benchmark soc.market_odds from stage s6 and from settlement_contract coverage (now m.rules_text only) and removed m.rules_text and soc.market_odds from the referee dataset feeds; soc.market_odds remains audited BENCHMARK_ONLY.

findings.text: Altitude definition is inconsistent. The measurement sets the effect to zero below a 500 m gap ('max(0, alt_gap - 500)/1000'), interaction #2 says altitude adds to home advantage 'only above roughly 1,500 m of gap', and nonlinearity #2 says 'Piecewise linear above 1500 m, saturating by 3000 m'. These imply different features; the record should fix one breakpoint and mark it as hypothesis. The 0.3-0.5 goal altitude effect in s3 is also unsourced.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Fixed one altitude breakpoint (500 m gap, saturating near 3000 m) in interaction 2 and nonlinearity 2 to match the input measurement and labelled breakpoints and the effect size as hypotheses to be fitted.

findings.text: environment category cites only altitude and rest_travel and the note says 'weather in other archetypes', which defers rather than declares a gap (heat/humidity/pitch are not covered by any input here). soc.referee is audited WEAK but is the only input for officiating_rules and for stage s5 (penalties ~0.3 per match, red cards ~0.1); the recorded penalty-rate input (soc.penalty_rate) is not attached. soc.second_leg_aggregate_state is used in stage coverage but is not defined or audited here.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Attached soc.weather (with a weather/pitch required_data row) to stage s3 and environment coverage, and soc.penalty_rate to stage s5 and officiating coverage so the WEAK soc.referee is not sole cover; noted that soc.second_leg_aggregate_state is catalog-defined but unaudited here.

findings.text: Lineup surprise logic is market-contingent: s2 says 'The market already prices the expected XI, so the informative quantity is the deviation of the actual lineup from the predicted one', and nonlinearity #3 says bad surprises count more 'since the market expects the star by default'. As a mechanism statement for a model that does not take prices as inputs, the effect is the actual XI quality; the 'surprise' construction is a feature for edge detection, not for outcome prediction, and the asymmetry claim has no support. The predicted-lineup history is also unavailable (disclosed as DATA_UNAVAILABLE), so a primary input cannot be backtested.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Removed the market-pricing framing from stage s2 and nonlinearity 3, recast soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted as a secondary timing/edge construct (not backtestable per rotation_timing) with outcome effect carried by soc.xi_strength_delta, and labelled the asymmetry as a hypothesis.

findings.text: Coverage: 172 GAME series span dozens of competitions (Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, Argentina, APF, Liga Expansion, Serie C and club friendlies are sampled). Data rows list Understat/football-data.co.uk/ClubElo as free sources for xG and results; none of these verifiably cover most of those leagues and there is no unresolved item for league-level source coverage. The two-way winner family is disclosed as unverified (good).
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:league_source_coverage

player_award.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the single sampled text (Women's Ballon d'Or 2025-26: Yes if the named player wins; ties split $1/n unless a Tie market exists; no award means all No; settles on the official announcement): (1) eligibility window and shortlist (30 nominees) narrow to 3-6 realistic candidates; (2) team trophies in the window (Champions League/major finals) as the dominant utility term, with year effects (tournament vs non-tournament year); (3) individual production and narrative within a trophy tier; (4) finite voter panel aggregation (points scale, home-country bias, noise) producing win and tie probabilities; (5) information flow: precursor awards, shortlist/ceremony cues and leaks; (6) contract mechanics (co-winners, no award). Critically, markets exist while the season window is still open, so remaining-season performance, availability and trophy-final probabilities matter for early prices and only collapse to nothing after the window closes. Required inputs: trophy/finalist state, production and role, precursor awards, panel model, leak signal. The record matches 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 well. What differed: it declares season-state inputs IRRELEVANT because 'the season window has closed', contradicting its own comp_sim 'before the final matter' and any pre-window pricing; the primary narrative input has no raw data; sample-size limits for fitting year-weighted trophy effects are undisclosed; the points scale has 11 values for a top-ten ballot.

findings.text: Horizon contradiction behind several IRRELEVANT verdicts. soc.player_minutes_expectation, soc.injuries, soc.finishing_regression, soc.leader_race_state and soc.shots are all audited IRRELEVANT because 'the season window has closed' / 'cannot affect a vote on a completed season', and s5 states 'Injuries and availability matter only before the window closes, so most existing season-stat inputs are inert'. But the only sampled market is a finalized one; sibling awards (KXBALLONDOR men's, KXSUPERBALLONDOR, KXPFAPOY, KXEPLPOY, KXWCAWARD in the other bucket) are listed with months of lead time, and the record keeps comp_sim as KEEP_SECONDARY ('Team trophy probabilities before the final matter'). Both cannot hold. The record must state the pricing horizon; if markets trade before the final, a candidate's remaining minutes, injury risk and final-contribution probability are live inputs (and a World Cup year shifts the window to June-July), so IRRELEVANT is wrong and should be 'inactive after window close'.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Changed IRRELEVANT verdicts for soc.player_minutes_expectation and soc.injuries to KEEP_CONTEXT (live while the window is open) and finishing_regression/leader_race_state to WEAK, attached minutes and injuries to stage s3, rewrote the s5 claim and recorded pricing_horizon_unknown.

findings.text: Primary input without data. soc.award_voting_narrative is KEEP_PRIMARY ('the conditional-logit on goals, trophies and media share is the right shape'), yet no required_data row contains a media-share, press-coverage or narrative field (the vote-table row has award, year, candidate, rank, points, club, country, trophies; the performance row has goals, assists, team_trophies, ucl_final_contribution). The same applies to the 'story' factors in s3. Either add a media-attention dataset (and an access class) or demote the input to context and list the gap. Also soc.award_vote_distribution and soc.comp_sim are model outputs/engine rather than raw inputs and are labelled primary/secondary inputs.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Added a media-attention required_data row (GDELT, Wikipedia pageviews, Google Trends) feeding soc.award_voting_narrative, demoted that input from KEEP_PRIMARY to KEEP_SECONDARY, relabelled soc.award_vote_distribution and soc.comp_sim as model output/engine (secondary), and logged narrative_signal_validity.

findings.text: Undisclosed identifiability limit. soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year is primary and is to be fitted by ridge conditional-logit with leave-one-year-out CV on '2018-2025 ... male and female plus Super Ballon d'Or' with several features and year interactions. The Women's Ballon d'Or has about 7 usable ceremonies since 2018 (none in 2020) and the points-scale/voter-panel features change over time, so a model with a tournament-year interaction is under-identified; the unresolved list has no entry for sample size or for regime changes (season-based window adopted recently, scoring scale). The data row also claims '15 years of Ballon d'Or and related awards' for the women's award, which did not exist.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Corrected required_data history (women's award exists since 2018, about 7 ceremonies, none in 2020), restricted soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year to main effects plus one tournament-year dummy with ridge shrinkage, and recorded the sample-size and regime-change limit as unresolved award_sample_size_regimes.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED / factual: the panel simulation specifies ballots 'top-10 ranking ... points 15,12,10,8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1'. That is 11 point values for a ten-place ballot (to my knowledge the published scale is 15,12,10,8,7,6,5,4,3,1) and the voter count 'about 100' is stated for the Ballon d'Or generally, while the sampled contract is the women's award, whose panel size differs from the men's. The scale and panel size are not in the market text and are not backed by a cited source; they should be recorded as unverified.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Corrected the ballot scale to ten values (15,12,10,8,7,6,5,4,3,1) in soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model and variants, marked scale and panel size as unverified (women's panel smaller than the men's) and logged ballot_scale_panel_unverified.

findings.text: Interactions: #2 (panel_vote_aggregation_model x award_vote_distribution, 'threshold') describes a property of the aggregation model itself (win = sign of difference in totals) rather than an interaction between two measured inputs; #3 (leak signal x vote distribution, regime-switch) is a Bayesian update rule; #1 sets 'multiplicative' on a softmax utility that is additive in the stated model (utility = sum of weighted features). No test would distinguish these structures from a single softmax with trophy and narrative terms.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Replaced interaction 2 (an aggregation property) with a tournament-year x vote-spread conditional interaction, rewrote the interaction-1 test as an additive-versus-product likelihood contrast, and labelled interaction 3 as a reliability-weighted Bayesian update rather than a structural channel.

findings.text: Mapping/scope: the single sampled series (KXBALLONDORAWARD) is a Women's award, the record's inputs (UCL/World Cup trophies, UEFA POTY, Super Ballon d'Or history) are written for the men's award, and the sibling award series stay in player_season_leader_and_awards; the record notes the bucket split in variants but not that no men's award, PFA/EPL player-of-year or WC award is covered here. Contract nuance not raised: whether the official announcement can be amended/corrected (the ledger types this series 'rules_review_correction') is not discussed.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:announcement_correction
